Ecosystem Health Scoreboard Oct 2026 · run 01‑10

Monthly integrity sweep of the second-brain workspace — full-tree census through the Google Drive API, kernel-vs-memory drift check, credential scan, and a four-pillar score, run cloud-only with no laptop in the loop. First full recount after the 26 Sep efficiency cut, so this run sets a new baseline. Sanitised public scoreboard; the full private record, with every path and finding, lives on Drive.

The four-point gain is Cross-Pollination and Architecture: the 26 Sep efficiency cut purged the un-synthesised screenshot hoard that was the standing synthesis drag, folded ten knowledge bases into five, and left zero Google-native stubs in the tree.

Score trend · v3 scoring basis (full tree, Drive API)

Four v3-basis runs, 61 → 60 → 62 → 66 — the biggest monthly gain of the series, carried by the efficiency cut landing in the census. The gap to the 85 "runs unattended and trusted" ceiling is the standing hygiene work below.

1 · What this run did

Measured

  • Full-tree census through the Drive API, cloud-only — the laptop was never in the loop. Batched breadth-first over the whole workspace: 3,219 active files, 359 folders, 13.5 GB active (archive excluded from the score). First true full recount since the efficiency cut; prior months carried their counts.
  • Kernel-vs-memory drift check: CLEAR. The rules on disk and in the cross-surface memory floor agree in substance; the check ran against the live files, not the lagging project-doc snapshot.
  • Credential scan across the whole tree — the first-class security pass.
  • Four-pillar score recomputed from this run's census; every figure traces to an API pull, with the two high-value pillars recomputed rather than carried.

Published (create-only, nothing moved or deleted)

  • Private master record written to Drive with the full, unsanitised detail — paths, findings, the reversible archive list.
  • Dated history + scheduler snapshot appended as new files (the audit trail is never overwritten).
  • This scoreboard carried into the public repo and mirrored to the Drive handoff for the fallback publisher.
  • No autonomous delete, move, or rename — every cleanup is proposed as a list for a human to action by hand.

6 · Action plan · owner: operator

  1. Confirm the retired GitHub tokens are revoked at the provider.VERIFY No plaintext credential file exists anywhere on Drive (verified this run, tree-wide). What a cloud run cannot see is whether each token was revoked at GitHub — deleting a file does not revoke a token. Confirm at the provider; keep the durable fix (repo authorisation / the GitHub MCP path, not a plaintext file).
  2. Refresh the two claude.ai artifacts from an interactive session.THIS MONTH Scheduled cloud runs have no artifact tool, so the Ecosystem Health db-write and the Second Brain republish are owed to the next interactive session; the public site is fed by the repo handoff instead.
  3. Thin the duplicate tail.THIS MONTH The honest recount shows 98 duplicate-name groups (~48 MB of byte-identical copies), concentrated in a few version series and mirrored contract/plan trees. All reversible; proposed as a by-hand list in the private record.
  4. Keep nudging naming compliance toward the standard.WHEN CONVENIENT At ~52%, the drag is Vietnamese-named contract and drawing PDFs. Rename proposals stay a human action.
  5. Clear the by-hand hygiene list.WHEN CONVENIENT A duplicate output folder (the sanctioned GDSH exception, confirm intent), a stray superseded prompt and two PASSBOOK files loose at the outputs root, and the two empty governance folders remain. All in the private record; the audit will not touch files unattended.

The one human decision that is the bottleneck

Confirm the old GitHub tokens were revoked at the provider. No plaintext token file exists anywhere on Drive and the routines now authenticate through the GitHub integration rather than synced files — but a file deletion is not a revocation, and only you can see the token list. Everything else on this board is hygiene the system proposes but cannot execute. The month's real story is good: the efficiency cut did what it was meant to — the synthesis bottleneck that dragged the score for months is gone, ten knowledge bases are five, and the stub data-loss class is zero. The machine censused, scored, confirmed the cut, published cloud-only, and ran the KB update — nothing destroyed.

Sanitised scoreboard. It carries only the score, per-pillar RAG and deltas, trend, plain counts, guardrail PASS/FAIL, and the credential-scan count + PASS/FAIL. It never carries a secret value or path, a file or folder listing, a person's name, an inbox detail, a private financial figure, or an automation trigger URL — those stay in the private .md record on Drive.
